meta.about: Every user-facing string in Flare: app screens, permission prompts, push, Telegram bot, plain-text SMS, share sheet, link previews, website, privacy and accessibility statements. Read by src/lib/copy/index.ts and checked by scripts/copy-lint.mjs.

rules.ui: 12 words or fewer (message, title, label, hint, status, error, aria, placeholder, option, push, bot, share, og-title)
rules.prose: 25 words or fewer per sentence (website, statements, exports, og-desc)
rules.sms: 200 bytes UTF-8 or fewer, worst case (BR-CH-2)

variantNotes.privacy.coords: A = server holds spot coordinates until Gone (analyst decision 10, current requirements). B = OQ-1 adopted: coordinates only inside the sealed invite. B is in force: ADR-0009 adopted OQ-1.
variantNotes.og.link: safe = preview uses only what the server can read (count, not the invite). full = BR-CH-4 as written (invite line in the preview); needs the server to hold the six words in plain text, which the architect must approve.

og.site.desc.text: Snap where you are. If enough friends say yes, it's on. Open source, private, and it works with no signal.

og.site.imageAlt.text: A park at golden hour with a bench, maple leaves and a small flame.

og.how.desc.text: Snap where you are, friends say yes in private, and it lights when enough can come. If not, it gets smaller.

og.privacy.desc.text: What Flare keeps, where, and when it's deleted. Plus the limits we're honest about and a live deletion audit.

og.access.desc.text: Benches, restrooms and steps on every invite, a talking compass, and what we tested. Known gaps are listed too.

og.run.desc.text: Flare is open source. Run the app and the Gemma 4 model on your own laptop with Ollama.

site.hero.title.text: If enough friends say yes, it's on.

site.hero.lead.text: Snap where you are. Friends get a six-word invite and answer in private. It only happens if enough say yes, and nobody ever sees a no.

site.hero.fine.text: Seconds of screen. An hour outside.

site.how.s1.body.text: The photo develops like a print while an open model writes six words. Send the link to iMessage, WhatsApp or Telegram.

site.how.s2.body.text: Each yes grows the flame. Everyone sees the count, never the names. Add a condition like “only if Amor comes”.

site.how.s3.body.text: When enough say yes, everyone who's in gets the spot. A talking compass points to your friend, even with no signal.

site.home.readHow.text: Read how a Flare works, step by step.

site.home.readAccess.gradeNote: A 6-word link. Accessibility is one 6-syllable word, and the word people search for.

site.shrink.lead.text: Plans stall in group chats. Flare plans get smaller.

site.shrink.kindling.text: Waiting for yeses, up to 30 min.

site.shrink.ember.text: No catch in 30 min? Then 15 min at the nearest bench. One friend is enough.

site.shrink.gone.text: “Not this time.” Same words for everyone. Then it's deleted.

site.shrink.plan.text: Plans for later come in four sizes, from a 60 min loop to 20 minutes on a bench. Anyone who's tired can quietly make it one step smaller.

site.how.gemma.text: Gemma is provided under and subject to the Gemma Terms of Use found at ai.google.dev/gemma/terms.
site.how.gemma.gradeNote: Required license wording, quoted word for word from the Gemma Terms of Use (docs/ml/model-selection.md).

site.privacy.p1.text: Photos are encrypted on your phone. The key is in the link, after the #, and never reaches our server.

site.privacy.p2.text: Conditions and access needs stay on your phone. Only rules like “back by 5 PM” are sent.

site.privacy.p3.text: There's no No button, so there's no no to show or store.

site.privacy.p4.text: Within 5 minutes of the end, the Flare, its photo and every yes are deleted. Only group counters remain, like how many came.

site.privacy.p5.text: No accounts, no ads, no trackers, and no fonts or scripts from other sites.

site.privacy.keepTitle.text: What we keep, and for how long

site.privacy.colWhere.text: Where, and who can read it

site.privacy.row.photo.what.text: Photo, six words, spot name, your first name

site.privacy.row.photo.where.text: Our server, sealed with the group key. Only people with the link can read it.

site.privacy.row.photo.when.text: Within 5 minutes of the end. Names go when you tap “Forget this group”.

site.privacy.row.yes.what.text: Who said yes, and their rules

site.privacy.row.yes.where.text: Our server, used only to decide if it lights. Never shown to anyone.

site.privacy.row.coordsA.where.text: Our server can read it. It uses it to pick a nearby bench and point the compass.

site.privacy.row.coordsB.where.text: Only inside the sealed invite. Your phone picks the nearby benches, so our server never reads it.

site.privacy.row.phone.what.text: Condition words, needs, walk requests, map photos, phone check

site.privacy.row.phone.when.text: When you clear them. Map photos go right after the draft.

site.privacy.row.sparks.where.text: Our server, sealed with the group key. Only your group can read them.

site.privacy.row.sparks.when.text: After 180 days with no meetups, or when the last person taps “Forget this group”.

site.privacy.row.alerts.what.text: Alert sign-ups and the Telegram link to your group

site.privacy.row.alerts.where.text: Our server, so it can send you the lit message.

site.privacy.row.counts.what.text: Group counters, like Flares sent and how many came

site.privacy.row.counts.where.text: Our server, under a random group id. No names, places, photos or words.

site.privacy.row.counts.when.text: Kept, so we can report how many people met.

site.privacy.row.logs.where.text: Our server. Never request bodies, photos, names, places, conditions or link keys.

site.privacy.l.telegram.text: Telegram sees what Flare posts there: a Flare card, the six words, the spot, the host's first name and the count. If your group turns photos on, Telegram also gets the photo and keeps a copy until the post is deleted. The post carries the Flare's link, so Telegram could open it too. The bot never reads your messages.

site.privacy.l.guess.text: In a small group, people can sometimes guess who said yes, or who made a plan smaller. With 2 or 3 people, the count alone can give it away.

site.privacy.l.sms.text: Text and satellite messages are outside our control. Your carrier and Apple carry them, and we can't delete them.

site.privacy.l.link.text: Anyone with the group link can read that group's invites, Sparks and Hot spots. Share it only with the group.

site.privacy.l.coordsA.text: Our server holds the spot's map position until the Flare ends, to pick a nearby bench and point the compass.

site.privacy.l.coordsB.text: Our server never holds the spot's map position. Your phone picks nearby benches and seals them into the invite.

site.privacy.l.hub.text: To write the six words, your photo goes to our laptop over an encrypted link. It isn't stored. If the laptop can't be reached, you type them and nothing is sent.

site.privacy.l.weather.text: When you make a Plan, your phone asks the US weather service for the forecast near you, to about 11 km.

site.privacy.l.push.text: Alerts travel through Apple's push service, sealed so Apple can't read them.

site.privacy.auditTitle.text: Deletion audit, after our Sunday field test

site.privacy.audit1.text: The audit runs after the field test on Sun Oct 11.

site.privacy.audit2.text: It counts leftover records in every store. Passing is 0.

site.privacy.audit.live.text: Live from our server, checked at {time}.

site.privacy.audit.fail.text: {n} leftover records past their delete time. We publish this as it is.

site.privacy.audit.down.text: The live audit can't be reached. Try again later.

site.privacy.audit.caption.text: Records past their delete time, per store

site.access.title.text: Built for friends with access needs

site.access.a1.text: Every invite shows benches, restrooms and mapped steps within 200 m of the spot.

site.access.a2.text: Set your needs once, on your phone. If a spot doesn't suit you, Flare counts you in for a closer one, and nobody learns why.

site.access.a3.text: The talking compass says “Fuego, 400 meters, slightly left.” No map to read.

site.access.a4.text: The invite photo has a spoken description of 20 words or fewer for screen readers.

site.access.a5.text: Bench to Bench prints a walking card in 18 pt type at 7:1 contrast, with a seat every 200 m.

site.access.target.text: Our target is WCAG 2.2 AA on every screen, body text at 7:1 contrast or more, and touch targets of 44 pt.
site.access.target.gradeNote: WCAG 2.2 AA, 7:1 and 44 pt are the standard's own terms; people checking the claim look for them.

site.access.t1.text: axe-core 4.14.0 on 193 screens and pages: 0 violations.

site.access.t2.text: Keyboard focus on 92 screen states: 0 touch targets under 44 px.

site.access.t3.text: 22 color pairs, checked indoors and in open sun: all pass WCAG.

site.access.g1.text: VoiceOver and the largest text size get tested on 4 real iPhones on Sun Oct 11. Until then, those results are not in.

site.access.g2.text: Map data can be wrong or missing. “No steps mapped” means none are in OpenStreetMap, not that the path has none.

site.access.g3.text: iPhone browsers can't vibrate, so the compass plays a short tone when you face your friend.

site.access.g4.text: Photo descriptions are written by an AI model and can miss things.

site.access.g5.text: The compass finds your friend. It isn't for navigation or emergencies.

site.access.why.text: Why benches: they raise the chance that an older adult with a mobility impairment goes for a walk from 60% to 75% (Netspar). 12.2% of US adults have a mobility disability and 5.5% a vision disability (CDC, 2022).
site.access.why.gradeNote: Cites two sources with their exact figures. Mobility disability and vision disability are the CDC's own category names, so readers can find the data.

site.access.feedback.text: Found a barrier? Tell us in the comments on our DEV post, and we'll fix it or list it here.

site.run.body.text: Flare is open source. The AI is the open-weight Gemma 4 model, run with Ollama on your own laptop, so no closed API sees your photos.

site.run.note.text: The repository link goes live when the repo is public. Setup steps are in the README.

site.run.needs.text: You need Node 24.21 or later. For the photo AI, use a Mac or any machine with a GPU, running Ollama.

site.run.s1.text: Install it, set one secret, and start the server and web app.

site.run.s2.text: In a second terminal, on the machine with Ollama, start the AI hub.

site.run.s3.text: Open localhost:8787/hello/ and pick a photo. Six words come back in about 3.5 seconds.

site.run.db.text: Postgres is optional for local runs. The tests use an in-memory Postgres.

site.run.license.text: License: AGPL-3.0 or later. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL. Model: Gemma 4, under the Gemma terms of use.

site.foot.made.text: Made for the DEV Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge, Week 1: Touch Grass.

site.foot.osm.gradeNote: Attribution wording the OpenStreetMap license asks for; it isn't ours to reword.
